dedupe_keys.name: simastir real time groundwater monitoring network costa rica

description: SIMASTIR, the real-time groundwater monitoring system of the Dirección de Agua, was started in August 2015 with the water utility AyA and the groundwater and irrigation agency SENARA to build an automated national network recording groundwater level, water temperature and electrical conductivity. The network has 44 monitoring sites in the aquifers Sardinal-Tempisque right bank, Nimboyores, Huacas-Tamarindo and Nicoya-Caimital and at the beaches Panamá, El Coco, Brasilito, Potrero and Cóbano-Montezuma. The stated uses are estimating aquifer supply, watching for saline intrusion, computing indicators, projecting water availability and assessing El Niño and La Niña effects. The technical data page offers reports with graphs of water levels and conductivity and a short analysis per aquifer. Coverage is priority aquifers of the North Pacific. Access is free as PDF reports on the website. Caveats: the only report linked is from June 2017, the raw series are not offered for download, and the project page says the network is still being reviewed. Simulation uses: groundwater supply and drought planning for coastal aquifers. Related records: Dirección de Agua geoservices (data-costa-rica-da-water-concessions-discharges-geoservices).
